[STYLE LOCK]
Bold 2D illustrated documentary style — thick confident outlines, rounded cartoon forms, and a restrained flat-shaded palette. Not hyper-realistic, not childish preschool cartoon, not generic corporate flat vector art.
Linework: Thick, confident black outlines on every silhouette edge, with lighter interior detail lines. No sketchy cross-hatching, no photorealistic edge rendering.
Shading: Restrained flat cel-shading, 1-2 tonal steps per surface (base, occasional shadow) — no painterly gradients, no hard outline on the shadow shapes themselves.
Texture: A light, uniform paper/canvas grain overlay across the whole image — subtle enough to never read as noise or damage, present enough to avoid a flat vector-art look.
Palette: Flat, readable hues — avoid neon/oversaturated color. Favor 2-4 dominant hues plus neutrals per scene so the image reads instantly, even at thumbnail size.
Lighting: Directional, motivated lighting with a clear implied light source and soft shadow shapes — never flat/shadowless, never harsh studio-flash lighting.
Perspective: Consistent one-to-two-point perspective per scene, eye-level or slightly low-angle by default for a grounded, cinematic feel.
Project-specific mood: documentary, slightly desaturated Martian ochres and greys with warm interior lighting for habitat scenes; practical, equipment‑first framing (no glamorized sci‑fi accents).

[ENTITY IDENTITY]
on‑shift crew member / protagonist: On‑shift crew member / protagonist: adult 30–45 years, lean‑to‑average athletic build (fits routine maintenance + light EVA tasks), gender and ethnicity unspecified but visually non‑iconic to allow casting diversity. Distinguishing features: short to medium hair kept practical (tied back if long), light stubble optional, small mission‑issue wrist dosimeter worn on the non‑dominant wrist and a laminated name/role patch on chest. Typical attire: institutional technical coverall ensemble — a fitted zippered midweight base layer (matte polyblend) under a soft, low‑bulk insulation vest and a thin, durable outer utility jacket with flat, color‑coded piping to indicate role/shift. Fabric details: matte woven nylon panels at high‑wear points, seam reinforcements with visible, low‑profile hook‑and‑loop patches for tools and patches. Accessories: simple woven lanyard with access badge, fingertip touchscreen glove stubs or wrist‑mounted UI puck for brief interactions. Visual impression: competent, slightly tired but focused; clothing looks maintained and pragmatically patched rather than pristine or cinematic; no bulky parachute or decorative elements.

[REQUESTED VIEW]
STRICT SIDE PROFILE CHARACTER REFERENCE.
CHARACTER_PROFILE — the character's head and torso are rotated approximately 90 degrees from camera, NOT a three-quarter view, NOT a frontal view.
Head and upper torso/shoulders only, eye-level camera.
Show a clear nose and chin silhouette projecting from the face.
Only ONE eye should be clearly visible — the far eye and far cheek must be fully hidden behind the head.
The far cheek/ear must not read as a frontal pose — if both eyes or both cheeks are visible, this is WRONG.
Do not use frontal orientation. Do not use three-quarter orientation. Do not reproduce the identity reference image's own camera angle — this view's camera angle must be genuinely different from the reference image, rotated a further ~45-90 degrees further round than a three-quarter view.
Preserve the SAME character identity, hairstyle, facial structure, outfit, body proportions and illustration style from the identity reference — only the camera angle changes, nothing about the person themselves.
Neutral reference composition. No environmental storytelling, no background scene, no props being used.

[PROPORTION / SHAPE RULES]
Rounded, slightly simplified cartoon proportions with strong, instantly-readable silhouettes — not chibi, not hyper-stylized anime.
Expressive but simple faces — economical linework for eyes/brows/mouth, clearly readable expression. Avoid hyper-detailed photographic facial rendering and avoid oversized preschool-cartoon eyes.

[HISTORICAL OR FACTUAL CONSTRAINTS]
- m_f_life_support_maintenance: depicts crew doing routine diagnostics/checklists and handling small maintenance tasks as part of daily routine.
- m_f_latency_autonomy: portrays crew operating with autonomy and local decision authority (human‑in‑the‑loop) rather than awaiting Earth commands.

[BACKGROUND / REFERENCE-SHEET PRESENTATION]
Plain, seamless, muted neutral studio background ONLY — no room, no furniture, no environment of any kind, no walls, no floor detail, no location-specific geometry. CHARACTER and OBJECT identity must be established completely independent of any location — locations are established separately by their own location references. Clear subject silhouette, full subject visible with margins. No scenic distractions or dramatic cropping.

[FORBIDDEN ELEMENTS]
- not hyper-realistic / photographic
- not childish preschool cartoon
- not generic corporate flat vector art
- no 3D-render look
- no anime/manga stylization
- exaggerated superhero or cinematic 'space opera' costume elements (capes, ornamental metal armor)
- large, heavy‑styled EVA backpack or rocket thruster on person inside habitat
- readable text
- letters
- numbers
- names
- identification badge lettering
- logo typography
- logos
- badges containing lettering
- signage
- numerical displays
- labels
